messages:
nina: Quick sync — I'm reviewing the connectivity contract language for on‑prem connectors. Customers keep asking for explicit firewall rules, static egress IPs, and an option for customer‑managed routing. Do we want a single packaging SKU with opt‑in managed features, or two explicit SKUs (lite: installer + port list, plus edge-agent add‑on for tunneled connectivity)?

emily: My read: split is cleaner for sales and support. 'Lite' keeps airgap-friendly installs simple and auditable. 'Agent add‑on' covers customers behind NATs or strict egress policies.

ryan: Technical constraints we should list up front: air‑gapped installers cannot call home; any managed tunneling requires a persistent outbound channel. For on‑prem we need clear KMS options: BYOK vs service‑managed keys.

kevin: From SRE/ops POV: we need a canonical firewall snippet. Prefer default deny with explicit allows. If we publish a single port list customers can copy into corp FW templates. Also recommend a TLS fallback (443) for regions that block uncommon ports.

emily: Draft port list (proposal):
```
- Outbound TCP 443 to updates.redwood-inference.com (optional for managed updates)
- Outbound TCP 443 to telemetry.redwood-inference.com (opt-in)
- Inbound TCP 2200 (optional, agent access)
- UDP 123 (ntp) or documented alternative
```
Note: for airgap, all outbound to redwood domains must be disabled — installer will accept local bundle.

nina: Nice. Now about contract language: customers want liability/exit language if they run customer‑managed routing that breaks. We should add a clause: "Customer responsible for maintaining firewall and network configs; Redwood will provide documented templates and support playbooks." Thoughts?

ryan: Agreed. Also include a troubleshooting SLA: if managed tunnel goes down we auto‑failover to queued mode and surface a support ticket. For on‑prem we need a clear escalation path (NetOps -> SE -> SRE).

kevin: Add checklist item: cert rotation automation and an emergency revoke flow. Docs should include sample cert rotation commands and a small script.

deploy-bot: New doc created: https://redwood-internal/docs/private-deploy/networking-contracts-draft (author: emily)

emily: Proposed launch criteria (for initial GA):
- Airgap installer validated in 3 partner environments
- Published firewall + port snippets and KMS integration guide
- Edge Agent alpha with NAT traversal tested and perf numbers < 200ms median handshake for our tunnels
- Support playbook and runbook for recovery scenarios
- Legal signoff on contract clause for customer‑managed networking

nina: That works. Prioritization: ship 'Lite' (installer + port list + BYOK docs) in Q1 of the cycle; ship 'Edge Agent' as an add‑on in Q2 after two pilot customers. Pricing/packaging TBD, but sales wants clear checkbox add‑ons.

ryan: Action items: I will spike a NAT traversal prototype (reverse TLS tunnel + heartbeat) and share perf + failure modes by next Wednesday (1941270000).

emily: I'll iterate the docs and the port list, and get legal feedback on the contract clause by end of week.

kevin: I'll draft the SRE runbook and cert rotation scripts, add them to the support repo. Also will prepare a minimal RFC for the firewall snippet language.

nina: Great. Final note: if any customer absolutely requires static public IP egress, we need a deterministic guidance doc: we can support reserved egress addresses only on Dedicated/Private with an extra infra fee. Call that out explicitly to avoid surprises.

emily: +1. I'll add a short callout in the FAQ and the sales one‑pager.

kevin: :thumbsup:

nina: Thanks all — will follow up with a short PRD link once emily's draft lands.

emily: PRD link posted: https://redwood-internal/prd/private-deploy/network-connectivity-v1 (incoming)

ryan: ack, I'll subscribe to the doc and drop perf notes there.

kevin: ack

nina: closing the thread for now, ping @channel if anything blocks.
